raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
> **Needs AITER >= 0.1.27** (ROCm/aiter#6369, `QuickAllReduceInt4.allreduce_rmsnorm`). It is called directly, with no fallback. Draft until `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` pins it.

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

FlyDSL INT4 QuickReduce is the INT4 path since #59478, but with `fuse_allreduce_rms` on it ran the prefill all-reduce and then a separate add-RMSNorm. AITER v0.1.27 adds the add-RMSNorm epilogue to the FlyDSL kernel; this routes the payload through it when FlyDSL takes it. #61020 builds on this PR to also fuse the MXFP4 activation quant.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for "FlyDSL QuickReduce RMSNorm", "quick reduce rmsnorm" and "flydsl allreduce". #56326 fuses AR + RMSNorm + per-token FP8 quant in the custom all-reduce kernel, and #55917 adds a plain FlyDSL all-reduce for RDNA4; neither touches the QuickReduce path.

## Claims

- With INT4 QuickReduce on, `fuse_allreduce_rms` takes the fused FlyDSL kernel for the prefill all-reduces the fusion pass covers (up to 4096 tokens at hidden 8192; see Limitations). The "fusion does nothing" warning from #59478 is gone.
- `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8, MI355X, `max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, two runs per arm, against main with the same flag: **mean TTFT -1.2% geomean** (-0.7% without the noisiest point), output throughput +0.5%, mean TPOT -0.3%. Most prefill chunks at 8192 tokens are above the pass's range, which is why the effect is small. Stacking #57547, which lifts that range, gives TTFT -2.2% and throughput +0.6% geomean.
- GSM8K (greedy, 1319 problems) is unchanged: C vs B flips go both ways, exact McNemar p >= 0.09.

## Validation

**Unit tests.** 4x MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-335dd77b09161c5d63139b4e7ae51bb9928305b1` with the AITER v0.1.27 `aiter/ops/flydsl` tree laid over it, tests and tree from this PR rebased on `upstream/main` (96c80f8af7):

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/distributed/test_quick_all_reduce.py tests/distributed/test_aiter_rms_fallback.py
```

```text
2 failed, 48 passed, 1 skipped in 484.12s (0:08:04)
```

The two failures are `test_custom_quick_allreduce[test_target0-2-2-INT4]` and `[...-INT3]` (TP2 x PP2 graph QuickReduce, the HIP path); they fail identically on `upstream/main`.

- `test_flydsl_int4_should_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_gates_operands`: the fused call is declined outside the QuickReduce window, for an unsupported hidden size, an fp32 weight, a non-contiguous residual and with FlyDSL off.
- `test_rocm_aiter_fused_rmsnorm_uses_flydsl_int4_for_prefill`: `_rocm_aiter_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_impl` takes the FlyDSL path for a prefill-sized input, passes the kernel its operands (plain and Gemma norm), and never reaches HIP QuickReduce + RMSNorm.
- The existing fallback tests in `test_aiter_rms_fallback.py` gained the new method on their fakes.

**Serving path, TP8.** With print-only counters on `QuickAllReduce.fused_allreduce_rmsnorm` and `_unfused_allreduce_rmsnorm` (the first three calls and every 500th are logged), four long-prompt requests (3k, 7.5k, 7.5k and 20k tokens) hit the fused route on all 8 workers, including the 3k-token request's 47 MiB payloads, and the unfused route never. The per-worker fused count stayed below 8000. It would have passed that if the 7.5k-token prompts and the 8192-token chunks of the 20k prompt had been fused, so those chunks are outside the pass's range (Limitations).

**End to end.** 8x MI355X, `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-335dd77b09161c5d63139b4e7ae51bb9928305b1` (vLLM 0.33.0rc1.dev320, AITER 0.1.26) with the v0.1.27 `aiter/ops/flydsl` tree laid over it in every arm. Each server starts from empty vLLM, AITER and FlyDSL caches.

- **A:** main, `fuse_allreduce_rms: false` (one run).
- **B:** main, `fuse_allreduce_rms: true` (two runs). Decode all-reduces use the one-stage fusion; prefill uses FlyDSL all-reduce + separate RMSNorm.
- **C:** this PR, `fuse_allreduce_rms: true` (two runs).

C vs B is this PR; B vs A is what the flag does without it (+0.7% geomean throughput, largest at 8k/1k concurrency 4, +3.9%). Runs were interleaved B, C, C, B, A. Random dataset, `random-range-ratio 0.8`. Deltas are C vs B means of the two runs; negative TTFT and TPOT deltas, and positive throughput deltas, favor this PR.

| ISL/OSL | Conc | Mean TTFT (ms) B → C | Δ | TTFT run spread | Output tok/s A / B / C | Δ | Mean TPOT (ms) B → C | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8k/1k | 4 | 370 → 373 | +0.9% | 2.5% | 330 / 343 / 343 | +0.0% | 11.1 → 11.1 | -0.1% |
| 8k/1k | 8 | 449 → 448 | -0.3% | 1.8% | 505 / 511 / 511 | +0.0% | 14.9 → 14.9 | -0.0% |
| 8k/1k | 16 | 695 → 692 | -0.4% | 0.4% | 732 / 737 / 738 | +0.1% | 20.5 → 20.5 | -0.1% |
| 8k/1k | 32 | 1453 → 1464 | +0.8% | 1.4% | 1011 / 1017 / 1018 | +0.1% | 28.7 → 28.6 | -0.2% |
| 8k/1k | 64 | 2604 → 2598 | -0.2% | 0.9% | 1362 / 1367 / 1368 | +0.1% | 42.9 → 42.9 | -0.1% |
| 8k/1k | 128 | 6569 → 6563 | -0.1% | 0.6% | 1720 / 1729 / 1740 | +0.6% | 64.9 → 64.4 | -0.7% |
| 8k/1k | 256 | 12711 → 12679 | -0.3% | 0.7% | 2091 / 2095 / 2109 | +0.6% | 105.4 → 104.7 | -0.7% |
| 60k/600 | 4 | 3278 → 3272 | -0.2% | 4.3% | 137 / 140 / 140 | +0.1% | 22.6 → 22.6 | -0.0% |
| 60k/600 | 16 | 6616 → 6543 | -1.1% | 1.2% | 184 / 184 / 184 | +0.3% | 74.3 → 74.2 | -0.2% |
| 60k/600 | 64 | 25276 → 25009 | -1.1% | 0.6% | 211 / 207 / 209 | +1.3% | 260.7 → 257.1 | -1.4% |
| 128k/1k | 4 | 8997 → 8490 | -5.6% | 13.7% | 98 / 99 / 101 | +2.3% | 30.3 → 29.9 | -1.3% |
| 128k/1k | 16 | 17825 → 16774 | -5.9% | 8.3% | 127 / 127 / 127 | -0.1% | 105.7 → 107.0 | +1.2% |
| **Geomean** | | | **-1.2%** | | | **+0.5%** | | **-0.3%** |

TTFT is lower at 10 of 12 points, but the 8k/1k deltas (-0.4% to +0.9%) are inside their 0.4 to 2.5% run spread, and 60k/600 concurrency 16 and 64 (-1.1%) are at or just beyond it (1.2% and 0.6%). The 128k points (-5.6% and -5.9%) have 8 to 14% spread between runs of the same arm, so they carry no signal. Throughput and TPOT move beyond their spread only at 8k/1k concurrency 128 and 256 (+0.6%).

**Accuracy.** GSM8K, 5-shot, greedy (temperature 0), 1319 problems (1314 scored in every run), same seed in every run, `sglang.test.run_eval`. Exact McNemar on per-question results:

| Pair | Accuracy | Only first right / only second right | p |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 vs B2 (same arm) | 0.9650 / 0.9703 | 2 / 9 | 0.065 |
| C1 vs C2 (same arm) | 0.9718 / 0.9703 | 8 / 6 | 0.79 |
| B1 vs C1 | 0.9650 / 0.9718 | 7 / 16 | 0.093 |
| B1 vs C2 | 0.9650 / 0.9703 | 6 / 13 | 0.17 |
| B2 vs C1 | 0.9703 / 0.9718 | 10 / 12 | 0.83 |
| B2 vs C2 | 0.9703 / 0.9703 | 10 / 10 | 1.0 |

A scores 0.9703. Two runs of the same arm differ as much as B and C do; there is no directional change.

**Reproduce:**

```bash
AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 \
VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MAX_SIZE_BYTES_MB=512 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 --trust-remote-code --gdn-prefill-backend aiter_flydsl \
  --quantization-config.targets '{"*shared_expert*": "mxfp4", "*linear_attn.in_proj_qkv": "mxfp4", "*linear_attn.in_proj_z": "mxfp4", "*linear_attn.out_proj": "mxfp4"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"splitting_ops": [], "pass_config": {"fuse_rope_kvcache": true, "enable_qk_norm_rope_fusion": true, "fuse_allreduce_rms": true}}'
# arm A: "fuse_allreduce_rms": false

# one point; the rest are listed below the block
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0.8 \
  --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 128 --warmup-requests 32 --seed 4 --request-rate inf

python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-threads 64 --num-shots 5 --num-examples 1319 \
  --temperature 0 --max-tokens 2048 --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'
```

<details>
<summary>All 12 points (seed, concurrency, prompts; warmup requests = concurrency)</summary>

| ISL/OSL | (seed, concurrency, prompts) |
|---|---|
| 8192/1024 | (1, 4, 32), (2, 8, 64), (3, 16, 96), (4, 32, 128), (5, 64, 256), (6, 128, 384), (7, 256, 768) |
| 60000/600 | (8, 4, 32), (9, 16, 96), (10, 64, 256) |
| 128000/1024 | (11, 4, 32), (12, 16, 96) |

</details>

## Details

**Before.** With FlyDSL QuickReduce owning a payload, `_rocm_aiter_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_impl` ran FlyDSL all-reduce plus a separate add-RMSNorm, so `fuse_allreduce_rms` did nothing for the prefill-sized all-reduces FlyDSL is fastest on.

**After.** On the non-one-stage branch, `_rocm_aiter_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_impl` asks `QuickAllReduce` first:

- `should_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm(inp, residual, weight)` accepts the call when `all_reduce` would run the payload through FlyDSL (`uses_flydsl_int4`), the kernel supports the hidden size (`QuickAllReduceInt4.supports_rmsnorm`, owned by AITER), and the residual and weight are bf16, contiguous and 16-byte aligned. It reads only tensor metadata, so it adds no host-device synchronization.
- `fused_allreduce_rmsnorm(...)` runs the fused kernel and returns `(out, residual_out)`, with Gemma (`1 + weight`) norms supported.

Decode sizes, which the one-stage custom all-reduce owns, keep their path. A payload FlyDSL takes but the kernel declines keeps #59478's unfused all-reduce + RMSNorm. The methods live on `QuickAllReduce` because it already owns the FlyDSL object. +53 / -17 non-test lines.

**Limitations and CI gaps**

- **Prefill coverage.** The fusion pass's range stops at the custom all-reduce's 64 MiB limit (4096 tokens at hidden 8192 in bf16). With `max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, chunks of 4097 to 8192 tokens keep the unfused path. #57547 (open) lifts the limit; with it applied in both arms the same sweep gives TTFT -2.2% and throughput +0.6% geomean, and the 128 MiB payloads of 8192-token chunks take the fused route.
- **Arms.** B and C both enable the one-stage decode fusion that the flag turns on, so C vs B isolates this PR; B vs A is reported separately. A is a single run.
- **Coverage.** Measured on gfx950, TP8, one model. The AITER kernel admits gfx942 but was tested only on gfx950. TP2/TP4 end to end and a second model are not run.
- **CI.** The unit tests run in the MI355 "Distributed Features" step. The end-to-end runs need 8x MI355X and the 2.4T checkpoint, so they ran outside CI.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

- `should_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm(inp, residual, weight)` accepts the call when `all_reduce` would run the payload through FlyDSL (`uses_flydsl_int4`), the kernel supports the hidden size (`QuickAllReduceInt4.supports_rmsnorm`, owned by AITER), and the residual and weight are bf16, contiguous and 16-byte aligned. It reads only tensor metadata, so it adds no host-device synchronization.
- `fused_allreduce_rmsnorm(...)` runs the fused kernel and returns `(out, residual_out)`, with Gemma (`1 + weight`) norms supported.

Decode sizes, which the one-stage custom all-reduce owns, keep their path. A payload FlyDSL takes but the kernel declines keeps #59478's unfused all-reduce + RMSNorm. The methods live on `QuickAllReduce` because it already owns the FlyDSL object. +53 / -17 non-test lines.

**Limitations and CI gaps**

- **Prefill coverage.** The fusion pass's range stops at the custom all-reduce's 64 MiB limit (4096 tokens at hidden 8192 in bf16). With `max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, chunks of 4097 to 8192 tokens keep the unfused path. #57547 (open) lifts the limit; with it applied in both arms the same sweep gives TTFT -2.2% and throughput +0.6% geomean, and the 128 MiB payloads of 8192-token chunks take the fused route.
- **Arms.** B and C both enable the one-stage decode fusion that the flag turns on, so C vs B isolates this PR; B vs A is reported separately. A is a single run.
- **Coverage.** Measured on gfx950, TP8, one model. The AITER kernel admits gfx942 but was tested only on gfx950. TP2/TP4 end to end and a second model are not run.
- **CI.** The unit tests run in the MI355 "Distributed Features" step. The end-to-end runs need 8x MI355X and the 2.4T checkpoint, so they ran outside CI.
